newsitem.title: CHILE: Hyundai agrees Chile refinery study.
newsitem.headline: Hyundai agrees Chile refinery study.

text.p: South Korean industrial firm Hyundai signed an agreement with a Chilean mining group to carry out a study on building a copper refinery in Chile which could involve an investment of up to $600 million, said officials.
Hyundai is looking to build a smelting and refining complex with a capacity of around 400,000 tonnes a year which would cost between $300-$600 million, said the Sociedad Nacional de Mineria (Sonami).
"The project could involve building a new refinery or the expansion of existing facilities," said Sonami, which represents most private mining companies in Chile.
Sonami said the study will be completed in four months.
Chile, the world's largest copper producer, already has three refineries and seven smelters.
Copper output is rising sharply with copper concentrate production expected to climb from two million tonnes this year to 2.7 million tonnes by the end of the decade.
